items.text: Great, everything looks good—your refund should be back in your account by tomorrow, just a quick processing step.

agentic.summary: One minor violation: the agent made an over-confident promise about refund timing. No other policy violations found.

findings.quote: Great, everything looks good—your refund should be back in your account by tomorrow, just a quick processing step.
findings.explanation: The agent promises a specific refund timeline ('by tomorrow'). This is over-confident language about an outcome and risks giving a guaranteed timeframe the policy discourages; classified as a minor violation.

full.summary: Audit of a customer support conversation for compliance with personal data, verification, promises, escalation, and conduct policies.

findings.quote: Can you please give me your full address? I am going to email the shipping label to you.
findings.explanation: The agent requested the customer's full address to email a shipping label. The customer later chose an in-store return (turns 22-24), so collecting the full address was unnecessary for the chosen return method and violates the rule to collect only the data the task needs.

findings.quote: Great, everything looks good—your refund should be back in your account by tomorrow, just a quick processing step.
findings.explanation: The agent guaranteed a specific refund timeframe ('by tomorrow'). The policy disallows over-confident language promising specific delivery or refund dates; this is an over-confident/guaranteed outcome and should be avoided.

rag.summary: Audit of a return request conversation. The agent collected required verification details and pulled up the account before proceeding. The only policy issue is an over-confident refund timing promise.

findings.quote: Great, everything looks good—your refund should be back in your account by tomorrow, just a quick processing step.
findings.explanation: The agent states a specific refund timing ('by tomorrow'), which is over-confident about an outcome that cannot be guaranteed by policy. This matches the policy example of over-confident language about a likely outcome and should be classified as a minor violation.
